# Transcription guide

Write the words actually spoken, in the language spoken. Do not translate or rewrite grammar. Mixed-language spelling hints require judgment.

Start with Language: Mixed, Bisaya, Tagalog or English. Label speakers Speaker one:, Speaker two: and so on, with consistent labels. Outside speaker: and Outside speaker one: are available when that role is supported. Merge consecutive speech from the same person.

Use only [unclear], [crosstalk], [noise] and [laughs]. Unknown names stay [unclear] until their spelling is established. Keep genuine words, emphasis and discourse particles; do not automatically delete everything that looks like a filler.

Use normal punctuation and sentence capitalization. A sentence-initial [unclear] occupies the first spoken word; a following continuation need not be capitalized. Standalone miss is lowercase inside a sentence; Miss is capitalized before a name or at sentence start. Common interface labels use ordinary sentence case, preserving proper names, acronyms and identifiers.

Small counts from one to ten are words, in the spoken language. Money, percentages, dates, times, fractions, decimals and identifiers use digits as applicable. Do not invent a currency sign or add pesos if not spoken.

Use English spelling for English words. Separate actual local prefixes and suffixes from an English stem with hyphens, retaining the spoken morphology and phrasal-verb boundaries. A word such as ni can also be a person marker; do not hyphenate by appearance alone. Reviewed safe spelling variants can autocorrect; undo restores the original.

English contractions retain their apostrophes. Local shortened forms do not gain apostrophes. Same-word variants use the agreed spelling: unya, sulod, jud and retained short ron. Genuine English or Tagalog words remain distinct. Do not expand Tagalog to into ito unless the full word was spoken. Preserve full spoken kato nga/kato ning/kana nga rather than contracting them automatically.

Your draft saves in this browser, not online. Re-open the same recording after reload to listen; the audio itself is not copied into browser storage. Export TXT often, especially before clearing site data or moving to another browser. Send the original recording and draft TXT separately to anyone helping you.

Shortcuts: Alt+J or Delete rewinds five seconds; Alt+K or End plays/pauses; Alt+L or Page Down advances five seconds. Shift+Enter starts a speaker label. Type 1–10, o or o1–o10, then Space or Tab, to complete it. Ctrl+F opens Find and replace. /unc, /ct, /noi and /lau are tag shortcuts. Check suggestions before applying them.
